brief: The parts of the job that never make the job description

slots.eyebrow: On the work behind the work
slots.title: Nobody hires you for
slots.subtitle: Six things that decide whether the work lands, none of which appear in a brief, a contract or a job description.
slots.idx1: Reading a brief that describes the wrong thing
slots.idx2: Showing work before it is ready
slots.idx3: Saying it went wrong before anyone finds out
slots.idx4: Handing over something that runs without you
slots.idx5: Being the person nobody has to chase
slots.idx6: Why none of it saves weak work

slots.title: Most briefs describe a solution, not a problem
slots.body: A client arrives with the answer already chosen, and the useful work is getting back to the question without making anyone feel corrected.
slots.p1Body: Not what they want built. What is different in their week once it exists.
slots.p2Title: Find the deadline behind the deadline
slots.p2Body: There is usually a board meeting, a launch or an investor behind the date.
slots.p3Body: In your words. If they correct you, you learned something for free.

slots.title: Showing work early is a skill, not a personality trait
slots.body: Everyone agrees with it and almost nobody does it, because an unfinished thing feels like evidence that you are not good enough yet.
slots.p1Title: Show the direction, not the polish
slots.p1Body: Rough enough that changing it costs nothing, clear enough to argue with.
slots.p2Title: Say what you want feedback on
slots.p2Body: Unbounded feedback is how a colour discussion eats a structural one.
slots.p3Title: Book the review before you need it
slots.p3Body: A date in the calendar is the only thing that reliably ends a draft.

slots.title: The recovery is remembered longer than the mistake
slots.body: Almost every relationship that survived a serious error survived because somebody said it out loud first, before it was discovered.
slots.p1Body: The cost of a problem doubles roughly every day nobody is told about it.
slots.p2Title: Bring the fix, not the apology
slots.p2Body: One sentence on what happened, three on what you are doing about it.
slots.p3Body: An apology without a changed process is a promise to do it again.

slots.title: Handing something over is part of making it
slots.body: Work that only you can run is not finished, it is a dependency wearing a deliverable's clothes, and everyone eventually resents it.
slots.p1Title: Write for the person after you
slots.p1Body: Assume they are competent, in a hurry, and have never seen this before.
slots.p2Body: The clever step that only works on your machine is the one that breaks.
slots.p3Body: Say nothing for ten minutes. It is the cheapest research there is.

slots.title: Being easy to work with compounds faster than being good
slots.body: Referrals rarely mention craft. They mention that you replied, that the date held, and that nothing had to be chased twice.
slots.p1Title: Reply before you have the answer
slots.p1Body: A holding message costs nothing and removes the anxiety entirely.
slots.p2Title: Never surprise anyone with a date
slots.p2Body: A slip announced in advance is a plan. Announced late, it is a failure.
slots.p3Body: Recommending someone else when you are wrong for the job comes back.

slots.title: None of this substitutes for the work being good
slots.body: Every one of these makes good work land harder. Applied to weak work they buy you a second project, and that is the whole extension.
slots.p1Body: It carries one project. The second one is judged on the first one's results.
slots.p2Body: A well-run project that produces mediocre work is still mediocre work.
slots.p3Body: The only defence against a rising bar is visibly clearing it more often.

slots.headline: Do the first one
slots.body: Ask what actually changes once the thing exists, and write the answer back in your own words. It takes ten minutes and it changes what you build.
slots.signoff: The rest keep until the project after
slots.quote: Every one of these is free. That is exactly why so few people bother with them.
